title: Where it breaks, by market
summary: Six markets as an unruled editorial index under a 72px heading: each market's name at the left, and at the right ONE sentence in one voice that carries the market's two traits and where it breaks there — the approved lines where they already carry both, each in its own shape. No label, codes, chips, toggles or paper.

reference.site: Kelwin's two-voice statement, applied to reading copy
reference.borrowed: An editorial index: the name, then one written sentence — no field structure.
reference.kelwin: Kit claim head (.ac-shead--claim, 72px) with no label over it; names in Mona display 32px; 20px sentences in --fg; graphite, because nothing here is a paper document.

motion: entrance: the kit claim head rises; the six entries rise 80ms apart (kit cascade) — the page's second (and last) body play-once moment.
interaction: none (all six read at rest).
on the live site: plays once as it scrolls into view. Reduced motion: final state.
story: Lets a buyer find his own market and its typical break before he reaches who is sent away.
copy: [K] heading 'Where it breaks, by market.' (the plan's §5 heading). No label (round 8's 'Six markets' restated the heading).

Enterprise SaaS — round-8 approved line, verbatim: 'The story that wins the champion dies in the committee, where every stakeholder carries a different version of what you do.' (champion and committee carry 'Sales-carried · Committee buys')

Cybersecurity — [R] before: 'Every vendor promises the same three outcomes in the same words. Differentiation is a language problem before it’s a product one.' → after: 'Every vendor promises the same three outcomes in the same words, to buyers paid to distrust them.' (folds 'Trust-gated'; drops the aphorism, an antithesis — plan §2 allows one per page and the plateaued 'deposits instead of evaporating' is it)
FinTech & payments — [K] verbatim: 'Compliance vocabulary smothers the actual story, and deals stall in risk review because nobody armed the champion.' (carries 'Regulated · Risk-averse buyer')

Developer & data infrastructure — [R] before: 'The buyer reads docs, not decks. Outbound only works when it sounds like engineering wrote it.' → after: 'Engineers try the product from the docs, and trust only what sounds like engineering wrote it.' (folds 'Technical buyer · PLG + sales'; keeps the docs and 'engineering wrote it'; drops the 'not decks' antithesis and 'outbound')
Professional & B2B services — [K] verbatim: 'Growth stalls where the partners’ networks end — the firm’s knowledge never became a sellable narrative.' (carries 'Relationship-led · Referral ceiling')

Industrial & deep tech — [R] before: 'Twelve-month deals drift: the narrative that opened the deal isn’t the one that closes it.' → after: 'Against legacy incumbents, twelve-month deals drift until the narrative that opened them is gone.' (folds 'Long cycle · Legacy incumbents'; keeps 'Twelve-month deals drift'; drops the 'isn’t the one' antithesis)

Cut: I·01–I·06, the 12 boxed mono chips, the open-in-place ledger, the paper surface, the round-8 lede ('Committee-decided deals make all three sharper' — the head lede already says committee), Dev & data's scope note (the PLG decline says it), the 'Six markets' label, the round-9 first pass's clipped trait pairs ('Trust-gated, in a crowded category.' …).
phone: ≤1023: names 26px in cols 1–5, sentences 18px in cols 6–12. ≤767: name (22px) over its sentence (17px), one column. Checked 834 · 390 · 320: no overflow; text-wrap: pretty.
notes: Words at rest: 119 (heading, names and sentences; the three ampersands not counted — 122 with them). Six sentence shapes: a where-clause, a trailing 'to buyers…', 'and … because', 'and trust only…', a dash clause, a fronted 'Against…' with 'until'. No antithesis in the section. No ruled list here — the page's one is the situations. Surfaces: the whole page is graphite with ruled seams; there is no paper document on this page (plan §7.5). Coherence pass 3: the services line loses its em-dash turn: “Growth stops where the partners’ networks end, because nobody wrote the pitch down.” (the section stays within its 120 words)
